tip: 'yüzyıllardır' means for centuries. The -dır ending on a time span shows how long something has been going on.
Negative future stacks -ma then -yacak on the verb: 'konuşmayacak' means will not talk. The -ma is the negative, -yacak the future.
'gezdirdiler' comes from 'gezmek' (to wander); the added -dir makes it mean show around. 'bize evi gezdirdiler' = they showed us the house.
The -meli in 'gelmelisiniz' means must or should. Personal endings come after it: 'gelmelisiniz' = you must come.
'gideceğimiz' describes the noun 'yer': the place we will go. Turkish puts this whole clause before the noun, with no word like which.
'kalkarsak' is the if form: 'kalkar' plus -sak. 'eğer' only flags the condition and can be dropped, 'kalkarsak' still means if we get up.
To report a command, turn the verb into a noun plus possessive: 'kalkmamı söyledi' means told me to get up, literally said my getting-up.
'yatmadan önce' means before going to bed: verb plus -madan önce is the before-doing pattern, and the verb stays in its base form.
For a reported statement Turkish turns the verb into a noun: 'olduğunu söyledi' means said that it was. The inner subject 'filmin' takes the -in ending.
Unreal past condition: 'olsaydık' means if we had been, paired with 'olmazdı', would not have happened. Both look back on what did not occur.
'yapmam lazım' means I need to prepare: 'yapma' plus possessive -m plus 'lazım'. Swap the ending for who: 'yapman lazım' is you need to.
'bitiremedi' means could not finish: the -eme inside marks inability, unlike plain 'bitirmedi', which just means did not finish.
'katılmak' takes the -a/-e ending: you attend to something, so it is 'toplantıya', not 'toplantıyı', before 'katılmayacağım'.
'yağdığında' means when it snowed: verb plus -dığında builds a when clause. 'kar yağdığında' sets the time for the main verb.
'ettirdim' means I had it done, versus plain 'ettim' I did. The person doing the work takes the -e/-a ending: 'tamirciye', to the mechanic.
'ısınınca' means once it warmed up: verb plus -ınca marks as soon as or when, linking the two events in time.
'çalıştığım' means the one I work at: -tığım turns the verb into a modifier placed before 'şirket', with no separate word like that.
'konuşuyor olacağım' means I will be speaking: present -yor plus 'olacağım' gives an ongoing future action, not a one-time will speak.
'yapmayacak' is the negative future: the -ma marks not and -yacak marks will, so it means will not do.
'madem geleceksin' means since you are coming. 'madem' opens a given-that reason and usually pairs with a command or plan, here 'erken gel'.
'yapacağın iş' means the work you will do. The -acağın ending makes a future verb describe the noun 'iş' right after it, with no word like that.
'gelince' means when it comes or once it comes. Verb plus -ince links one event to the next, so 'yaz gelince' sets the time for the main verb.
'parkta' means at the park. The k in 'park' is voiceless, so the ending takes -ta, not -da: 'parkta', never 'parkda'.
'söylediğin' means that you said. The -diğin ending turns the verb into a modifier before 'her şey', so 'söylediğin her şey' is everything you said.
'yarından itibaren' means from tomorrow on. 'itibaren' needs the -dan ending on the time word, giving 'yarından' from 'yarın'.
'saat üçü çeyrek geçiyor' means quarter past three. For minutes past the hour, the hour takes an object ending, here 'üçü' (üç + ü), and 'geçiyor' means is passing.
'olacakmış' means it will be, going by what was heard. The -mış after the future -acak adds an apparently or reportedly to the prediction.
'maviye boyadı' means painted it blue. With 'boyamak' the resulting color takes -e, so 'mavi' becomes 'maviye'.
'temizlendi' means it was cleaned. The -n inside 'temizlemek' flips it so the shovel is acted on rather than doing the cleaning.
'gelene kadar' means until she comes. Verb plus -ene kadar marks until that happens, so 'annem gelene kadar' sets how long the studying lasts.
